# Clean up your writing with Copilot in seconds

**Hook**
You’ve just finished a report, email or blog post and you want it to look polished. Instead of reading every line yourself, let Copilot scan your text and suggest fixes for typos, grammar and style. In this guide you’ll open Copilot, paste your text, and get clean suggestions in under a minute — with no account needed.

## Before you start
- A computer or phone with a web browser
- A free GitHub account (join at [github.com](https://github.com))
- A short piece of text you want to improve (a paragraph or two is fine)
- About 5 minutes total

## Step 1 — Open Copilot in your browser
Go to [copilot.github.com](https://copilot.github.com) and click the big blue button that says **Start for free**. If you already have a GitHub account, sign in; if not, create one by following the prompts. After you sign in you’ll see Copilot’s chat window open in your browser.
You’ll know it worked when you see a chat box with a blinking cursor ready for your message.

💬 Example:
Just paste the link into your browser’s address bar and press Enter.

## Step 2 — Paste your text into the chat
In the chat box type or paste the instruction:
“Check this paragraph for typos, grammar and style.”
Then press Enter. Copilot will read your text and show a list of suggested edits right below your message.
You’ll know it worked when you see numbered suggestions appear under your prompt.

💬 Example:
Check this paragraph for typos, grammar and style.

## Step 3 — Review the suggestions
Look at each numbered suggestion Copilot gives you. If a suggestion is correct, you can copy it into your document. If a suggestion doesn’t feel right, you can ignore it or ask Copilot to explain why it suggested it.
You’ll know it worked when you can see clear, numbered edits that make your text read more smoothly.

💬 Example:
Copy the corrected sentence into your document.

## Step 4 — Ask for style improvements
If you want Copilot to make your writing more formal, concise or friendly, type:
“Make these edits more formal” or “Make these edits more friendly.”
Copilot will rewrite the suggestions to match the tone you asked for.
You’ll know it worked when you see a new set of edits that match the style you requested.

💬 Example:
Make these edits more formal.

## Step 5 — Copy the clean version back
After you’ve accepted the edits you like, copy the corrected text from the chat box and paste it back into your original document. Save the file and you’re done.
You’ll know it worked when your document reads clearly and you didn’t have to hunt for typos yourself.

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting a huge document** → Copilot may time out. Paste one paragraph at a time instead.
- **Ignoring suggestions without reading them** → Always glance at each suggestion; Copilot can catch things you miss.
- **Expecting perfect edits every time** → Copilot is a helper, not an editor. Use your own judgment before accepting changes.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Quickly polish a cover letter, social media post or school assignment before sharing it with others.
- **For your business or work:** Review client emails, reports or proposals to make sure they’re error-free and professional.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with short texts so you can see how Copilot works without feeling overwhelmed.

## Try it now
Open [copilot.github.com](https://copilot.github.com), sign in with your GitHub account, paste a paragraph you’ve written, and type “Check this paragraph for typos, grammar and style.” Copy the clean version back into your document and save it.
